newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - May 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - May 12.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Monday's electronic version of The Wall Street Journal:
* Fred Meyer Inc has agreed to acquire Smith's Food & Drug Centers Inc for $720 million in stock. It also has agreed to assume $1.3 billion of Smith's debt.
* Occidental Petroleum Corp are trying to determine whether it overpaid some foreign middlemen or if any money was used for foreign pay-offs, sources told the Journal.
* Ford Motor Co is considering going into business with dealers in three cities to create auto superstores.
* Engine plant workers at Chrysler Corp have voted to end their strike, allowing the company to resume production of light trucks.
* EchoStar Communications Corp DISH.O has sued News Corp Ltd over their aborted direct-broadcast television venture.
* Industry executives said Microsoft Corp is stepping up its plans to move beyond personal computers.
* Cephalon Inc and Chiron Corp said they are not giving up on their injection treatment for Lou Gehrig's disease despite an FDA panel's recommendation that it not be approved.
* Dow Chemical Co has won a court ruling that sends about 10,000 silicone-breast-implant cases filed in state and federal courts around the U.S. to a federal court in Detroit.
* Baesa, the Latin American bottler of PepsiCo Inc, said trading of its stock was halted in Buenos Aires after its quarterly results showed a negative net worth under Argentine accounting rules.
* The dollar has fallen to its lowest level since the beginning of the year.
* Pharmacia & Upjohn has named Fred Hassan as chief executive.
* United Steelworkers of America have ratified a contract with Goodyear Tire & Rubber Co, ending an 18-day strike.
* SBC Communications Inc and PacTel Corp, which recently merged, saw its quarterly net income drop by 3.5 percent.
* Privately held Nets Inc filed for bankruptcy-court protection.
* Investment banker Sean Crowley, the head of Smith Barney's media and telecommunications group, has left to join Merrill Lynch.

* Mobil Corp, Amoco Corp and DuPont Co sent representatives to an energy conference in Iran this weekend, underscoring the difficulty the U.S. government is having isolating Iran's petroleum industry.
* General Electric Co's NBS has agreed to pay the three co-stars of the comedy, "Seinfeld," $600,000 an episode, sources said.

* Heard on the Street: For years under former chairman Andrew Sigler, paper maker Champion International Corp lodged board members and held meetings on a multimillion-dollar estate near its Stamford, Conn., headquarters. Richard Olson has been Champion's chairman since last fall. And now the Treetops estate ... is up for sale.
* Credit markets: Two weeks ago, currency trades were laughing at attempts by the world's seven major industry countries to talk the dollar down. Now they're crying as the dollar tumbles.
((-- New York Newsdesk 212-859-1610))
